title: Split out subsections of "Event handlers"
body:
The event handlers section of the spec is big, and with the increased precision of #3850, it's getting bigger. It's kind of hard to follow, and I think one of the main culprits is lack of section breaks. It's hard to isolate your focus on just a concept or two at a time when there's no logical division; instead it's just this great mixed-together flow of definitions, algorithms, examples, etc., spanning both content and IDL attributes.

I briefly tried myself, but it turns out my initial hope of isolating all the complicated content attribute stuff was not possible, because Window event handlers aren't content attribute event handlers but still need the "get the current value of the event handler"/"internal raw uncompiled handler"/etc.

For anyone who wants to try harder than me, my structure was going to be:

- Event handlers
  - Introduction and definitions
  - Common infrastructure (target, event handler map, activate/deactivate)
  - IDL types
  - Event handler IDL attributes
  - Event handler content attributes
  - Remarks and examples
  - Event handlers on elements, Document objects, and Window objects
- Move "Event firing" section into [activation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#activation)
- Remove "Events" parent section; put "Event handlers" directly under 8.1 "Scripting"

The problem I ran into was that "Common infrastructure" ballooned too large and it was weird to have all that goopy technical stuff up front.

I can imagine versions that do better than this. Let's revisit this after #3850 lands.
 /cc @TimothyGu @annevk.
